chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Aban ibn Uthman from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the found object of the Sanctuary, and he said, 'Do not touch it at all until its owner comes and takes it.' I said, 'And if it is a large amount of wealth?' He said, 'If the owner is not like you (i.e., not particular about it), then let it be announced (as lost property).'

key_terms.يُعَرِّفْهَا: To announce it (as lost property so the owner can claim it)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for found objects in the Haram according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the specific ruling for *luqata al-haram* (found objects within the Sanctuary of Makkah), emphasizing a state of cautious preservation where the finder abstains from using the item until the owner appears. The Imam clarifies that for high-value items, mere possession is insufficient; the finder must actively announce the find to facilitate identification, reflecting the heightened sanctity and strict accountability of the Haram. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the holiness of the location imposes stricter duties of care and transparency on the finder compared to general found property.
